Test fixture data must be synthetic, public-domain, or otherwise cleared for repository use.

The deliverable exists to isolate the straight pipe element as one bounded solver feature slice, giving the global 3D frame solver a governed, testable element behavior while keeping section data, units, diagnostics, load hooks, and force recovery explicit.
Principle: keep mechanics computation separate from rule-pack acceptability and human compliance judgment.
Principle: treat dimensions, material values, and protected standard-derived values as external governed inputs, never public bundled defaults.
Principle: prefer explicit TBD and explicit diagnostics over silent assumptions when solve-required values are missing.
Principle: preserve unit and provenance information through element inputs and outputs.
Principle: keep weight behavior as an interface hook until the load-case contract determines how loads are formed and applied.

The element will likely depend on upstream contracts for section properties, units, domain objects, application-service result envelopes, primitive load cases, and solver kernel assembly; those contracts are not resolved in this setup pass.
Verification should use open, synthetic, or cleared test cases, and hand-check examples must avoid copying protected standard examples, tables, or protected formula presentations.
Trade-off (completeness vs data boundary): record missing section or material values as findings rather than providing public defaults.

Trade-off (element scope vs solver kernel scope): keep local element behavior here and keep global assembly, transforms, and sparse solve in the solver kernel deliverable unless the accepted boundary says otherwise.
Trade-off (load hooks vs load application): expose weight-related information without creating hidden primitive load behavior inside the element.
Trade-off (force recovery vs stress checks): recover mechanical element forces while leaving downstream stress recovery and rule checks to separate deliverables.
Concrete numerical examples are TBD; future examples must use synthetic or cleared data and must not reproduce protected standards content.

The deliverable specifies setup evidence for the future straight pipe element backend slice, covering local stiffness, section-property integration, weight hooks, and element force recovery within the global 3D centerline/frame solver architecture.
The setup pass does not implement solver code, edit repo-level modules, create test fixtures, introduce protected formulas or tables, or make certification/compliance claims.
DEL-04-02-RQ-001: the straight pipe element shall fit the 3D centerline/frame solver model and shall not bypass the solver kernel boundary (basis SOW-006, OPS-K-MECH-1, AB-00-02).
DEL-04-02-RQ-002: local stiffness behavior shall be derived only from open mechanics and user/project/lawfully imported input values (basis SOW-006, OPS-K-IP-1, OPS-K-DATA-1).

DEL-04-02-RQ-003: section-property integration shall require explicit section-property inputs or validated upstream calculations, and missing solve-required properties shall produce explicit findings (basis SOW-006, OPS-K-DATA-2, OPS-K-UNIT-1).
DEL-04-02-RQ-004: weight hooks shall expose the information needed for load-case application without silently applying hidden load defaults (basis SOW-006, OPS-K-DATA-2, AB-00-03).

DEL-04-02-RQ-005: element force recovery shall return unit-aware mechanical result components suitable for downstream stress recovery, without encoding code stress checks (basis SOW-006, OPS-K-MECH-2, OPS-K-UNIT-1).
DEL-04-02-RQ-006: solver changes shall include deterministic verification tests before release use (basis OPS-K-SOLVER-1, AB-00-08).
DEL-04-02-RQ-007: diagnostics shall use governed result-envelope concepts and shall not claim professional approval, certification, or compliance (basis AB-00-06, OPS-K-AGENT-4).
